chapter: Connie's Inn, Duke Ellington and the Swingland band
title: Skeleton piano parts with chord symbols to save time
summary: For broadcasts Horace gave pianists chord symbols, saying 'I Got Rhythm' one chorus, because copyists' copies weren't paid for.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: When we were talking the other day, you had said that in the beginning everything that you played was written out -- piano parts were generally written out. By this time again, 19 -- mid-thirties, were pianists still having everything written out? I mean on the stock arrangements, we do see them written, but what about your own arrangements?
Well, I used to make a skeleton piano part, because --

A lot of the things that -- like, for instance, when we'd play a thing like "I Got Rhythm", well I know that so I (inaudible) one chorus I Got Rhythm, and then just say, write it on the piano part modulate, you know, so and so, and I just (unintelligible) save time.

you wouldn't have the time to, you know, write out a real part, plus the fact that they weren't paying you for copyists copies during those days, and one of those things, so you had to find a short cut. And this was it.
That's sort of like Bach when he was writing a new cantata every week, you know, he had to borrow from other composers and other of his own music, and everything else.
